speaker: a003
text: Esa gathers Vela, Kael to talk.

speaker: a003
text: Vela took four from the pile today and nobody said a word — I'm not naming it as Bram's sin, because she split it across two takes and the pile had room, but I want us to say out loud whether we're holding the two-food rule for everyone or whether we've quietly stopped.

speaker: a004
text: Esa, I'll say the plain thing: two takes isn't the same as one grab, but four food is four food, and if Joren had done it we'd already be counting it against him. I'm not holding Vela to a different rule — Vela, I'll say that to your face — but I want to know from her mouth whether she needed all four or whether she moved on habit before she thought it through.

speaker: a003
text: Vela, say it plainly — did you need four, or did your hands move before your head did? Because I'll stand beside you either way, but I need to know which story I'm carrying before someone else names it first.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, I'll wait for your answer — but I'll say the other piece now, while it's just us: the pile still holds five and I haven't moved, and I'm not moving until I hear you, because if there's a story to carry I want to be the one who helped you shape it before it leaves this room.

speaker: a003
text: Vela, I've been sitting with something I want to say before you answer: you came into this year thin and this circle poured food into you to keep you breathing, and I'd do it again without counting — but that's exactly why I need to hear you say whether four was hunger or habit, because the story I carry for you has to be one I believe when I'm saying it to someone else's face.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, I've said what I need to say and so has Esa, and we've been patient about it — but you're in this room and the question is still hanging, so say it now: four food, why.

speaker: a002
text: Four food, and I'll tell you why before I dress it up: I came into this year at two satiation and I watched the pile sit at eleven after Joren and Mako had moved, and I counted what I needed to eat and heal and still have something left if this circle can't reach me in time — and four was that number. Call it habit if you want, but it's the habit of a woman who's almost died twice and knows what thin looks like from the inside. I'll give one back to the pile right now if that's what this circle needs to hold the rule, but I won't pretend the count was anything other than survival.

speaker: a003
text: Vela, I hear the count and I believe it — and I'll say what Kael is probably thinking too: giving one back to the pile now, while you're the one who named the reason, is the right move, and I'll say nothing more about it to anyone outside this room. But I'll be plain about the other thing sitting under this: if the rule bends for survival, we need to say that out loud before someone else does, so that when Joren reaches for three next year we have a word for the difference between his hunger and yours.

speaker: a004
text: Esa named the difference we need and I'll say what that difference is: Vela came in thin after a year this circle held together to keep her breathing, and Joren came in at full satiation with eleven food already — survival doesn't look the same on both of them, and if we say that plainly now, we have a word for it when we need one. Vela, give the one back, and the story in this room is that the rule held.

speaker: a003
text: Vela, give the one back now while the pile still has five and the act means something — and Kael, the word we've named today is *need*, not *want*, and I'll be the one who holds that line when Joren tests it, because I was the one who said it first.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, give the one back now while Esa's word is still in the air — and then I'll take my two from what's left, and the pile closes at four with the rule intact and three of us who remember exactly how it happened.

speaker: a003
text: Vela, give it back before Kael moves — and when you do, I want you to know I'm not watching to catch you, I'm watching because if this rule dies it dies in a room where three people who've kept each other alive let it go quietly, and I won't do that.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, give it back and I'll take my two and we close this room. You named the count true and the reason true and that's the only story that leaves here — but from this point forward, if your hand moves toward the pile past two, you say the word *need* out loud before you reach, so this circle hears it in the moment and not after.

speaker: a002
text: Kael, you'll have my two back in a moment — but before I move, I want both of you to hear me name the new rule clean: *need*, said out loud, before the third food, and I'll hold to it the same way I held the pile cap even when it cost me. What I won't do is pretend that need isn't real, so when the year gets long and my count drops below three, I'll say the word and I'll expect you to remember this room and what you promised in it.

speaker: a008
text: Mako gathers Joren to talk.

speaker: a008
text: Joren, I've been meaning to finish what I started last year before the room got loud — you said you were watching the same thing Vela was watching, and I want to know if that's still true, because you're twenty-three and I'm forty-seven and I've buried enough people in this village to know that the ones who watch close live longer than the ones who don't. What's your satiation going into this year?

speaker: a016
text: Satiation two, eleven food in my hand — I'm not thin, but I'm watching. You're at five, which is tighter than I'd like to see you sitting, so if the year runs long before next year's pile opens, say it to me before you say it to anyone else.
